title: Make a Payday Plan
blurb: Give each paycheque a job before it disappears.
cards: Start with money that actually arrives
Use take-home pay after deductions. If pay changes, start with a cautious amount you can rely on, then plan what extra income will do when it arrives.
List bills by due date, minimum debt payments, food, transport and other essentials. Set aside the amounts before deciding what is available for flexible spending.
Choose the best first step for each item.
A streaming add-on you might want
Extra shift pay not yet earned
Cover committed essentials first. Do not build today's plan around income that has not arrived.

1. Confirm take-home pay.
2. Cover essentials and minimum payments.
3. Move a planned amount to savings.
4. Set a realistic amount for flexible spending.
5. Leave a small buffer if possible.
What should your payday plan use as its starting income?
Take-home pay you can rely on
Take-home pay is the amount available to plan after deductions.
A bonus is uncertain. What is a safer approach?
Decide how to use it after it arrives
Keep recurring commitments affordable on reliable income. Make a plan for extra money once it is real.
